description: The Université Libre de Bruxelles research team publishes notebooks for dasymetric population mapping with GRASS GIS. The documented workflow redistributes census counts using very-high-resolution land-cover and land-use information and a random-forest procedure, illustrated for Dakar. Its public GitHub repository supplies Python notebooks and supporting instructions under the MIT licence, permitting free reuse. The method is globally transferable when suitable input data are supplied, while the accompanying example products cover Dakar at 100-metre resolution. Infrastructure simulation modellers can use the resulting population surfaces to allocate service demand or estimate infrastructure exposure. Local census quality and classification errors constrain the estimates, and execution was not tested. No directly related catalogue platform was identified.
name: Dasymetric mapping using GRASS GIS
notes: G4-0410; G4 other data journals. Metadata only. Simulation uses are reviewer assessments. Data payloads and code execution were not checked.  Language: Python.
